page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance configured with 2 vCPUs and 15.0 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, this server allocates 1 physical core with 2 threads per core at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The CPU features a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512). It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators.

Performance benchmarks reveal a stark contrast between single-threaded and multi-threaded capabilities. The instance achieves top-tier single-core performance in Geekbench and strong single-threaded compression and decompression speeds. However, due to its configuration of a single physical core, multi-core benchmarks are weak, with poor multi-core CPU performance in stress-ng and low multi-threaded Geekbench scores. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with uncached read and write speeds falling into the bottom decile of tested hardware.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c4-highmem-2 offers a low-cost entry point to access dedicated Intel Xeon resources with a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 7.5 GB per core. However, the resource density presents a clear tradeoff: while single-threaded execution is highly efficient, workloads requiring high memory bandwidth, parallel processing, or rapid database operations will face significant performance bottlenecks.

This instance is best suited for workloads that prioritize single-core execution speed and moderate memory capacity over parallel processing. Appropriate use cases include lightweight text processing, single-threaded data parsing, small-scale caching, and basic web serving where multi-threaded throughput is not a primary requirement.
